newsitem.title: OMAN: Jerusalem status can't be pre-empted - UK minister.
newsitem.headline: Jerusalem status can't be pre-empted - UK minister.

text.p: British foreign office minister Derek Fatchett said on Sunday the final status of Jerusalem could not be determined until the closing stages of negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

Israel insists Jerusalem is its indivisible capital, but the Palestinians want the largely Arab eastern part of the city to be the capital of the territory they administer. Both sides' reluctance to give ground on the issue is one of the biggest obstacles in the stalled Middle East peace process.

"The status of Jerusalem will be determined in the final stages of negotiations, it cannot be pre-empted, it cannot be pre-determined...We will hold to that position," Fatchett told a news conference in Muscat.
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down in March when the Jewish state started building a settlement in East Jerusalem.

Fatchett, who arrived in Oman on Sunday and was also due to visit the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait, is the first British minister to visit the Gulf since Britain's new Labour government took power last month.
"As a British Labour government, we will make any contributions that we can towards creating conditions in which it is possible to achieve a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace," he said.

"What happens in the Middle East is at our doorstep, therefore we have a profound interest, shared religions and shared cultures to a certain extent and we also need to enjoy shared peace and shared prosperity," he said.

Fatchett, who was received on Sunday by Oman's Sultan Qaboos, said Britain's cool stance towards Iran would not change as long as the Islamic republic continued to "support terrorism and undermine the (Middle East) peace process".
"Until these are changed, our current position on Iran stands," he added.
Iran denies sponsoring terrorism and says its backing for anti-Israeli groups gives support to a just and legitimate cause.
